bundleBudgets.unit: gzip bytes of each route's initial transitive local JavaScript, summed as scripts/report-bundles.mjs sums them (it prints KiB to one decimal)
bundleBudgets.base: 15949ec0 built the same two ways with vendor/zodiacs-engine-0.1.1-rc.10.tgz installed
explanation: No budget changed, and no route's initial JavaScript grew by more than 4 bytes: /birth-chart/ is 10 bytes smaller with production's flags and 9 bytes smaller with the defaults.

rc.14 renames the two package chunks the initial bundles share, its aspect table and its house arithmetic (chunk-FR5TX5ZG and chunk-N4WHSUFK became chunk-NAJ735VN and chunk-4OSOCZY2). With hashed file names and the version string set aside, every chunk of the initial bundles of /, /birth-chart/, /big-three/, /today/ and /compatibility/ in the default build is byte for byte the base build's; the new names compress a few bytes differently.
That is the whole of /compatibility/'s 4 bytes under the default flags (0 with production's): no code joined the page, so nothing could move behind a dynamic import.

src/lib/engine/progressions.ts and the package root entry it imports are reached only through ChartLens's await import(); they are in no route's initial closure, and the build reports no ineffective dynamic import for them.

The engine chunk, which pages load only when a chart is asked for, grew by 527 bytes: the package's chart chunk by 458 (mostly rc.13's error wrapper and rc.14's span check) and its ΔT chunk by 72 (Rolldown placed EPHEMERIS_SPAN there), less 3 bytes elsewhere. 345 bytes of its 27 KB budget remain.

limits: The site-output comparison is the site against itself on two archives, not a measurement against a reference.
The rc.11 to rc.14 APIs the site does not use (configured aspects, declinations) are not measured here; their evidence is the engine repository's.
Receipt and import conventions and trust behaviour are unchanged.
No push, merge, deployment, npm release or model-spending approval is implied by these checks.
